Integration branch for the imbue_cloud slice-fleet generation 2 program (raw qemu slices with routed-tap networking on Debian 13 boxes, replacing lima), merged together with `main` and the three pre-cutover fix PRs: imbue-ai/mngr-internal#857 (SSH certificates from Vault, #850), #855 (DHCP placement, #849) and #856 (the upstream artifact mirror, #851). The per-change details live in this directory's constituent entries, listed below.

The gen-2 operator tooling: box ordering/prep/setup for generation 2 (WireGuard management overlay, `:22` lockdown, box telemetry, DHCP server, CA-trust-only management SSH, mirror-sourced downloads), the `cutover` command group, `wireguard` and `artifacts` commands, and the per-tier operator identity directory `~/.mindsadmin/<tier>/`.

Constituent entries: `new-fleet-base.md`, `new-fleet-runsc-prototype.md`, `new-fleet-phase-2.md`, `new-fleet-phase-3.md`, `new-fleet-phase-4-impl.md`, `new-fleet-phase-5.5.md`, `mngr-variable-sizing.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-2.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-3.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-4.md`, `mngr-new-fleet-testing.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-canary-followups.md`, `mngr-finish-new-fleet-canary-testing.md`, `mngr-identify-new-fleet-issues.md`, `mngr-design-network-observation.md`, `mngr-onetun-install-and-canary.md`, `mngr-lima-rename.md`, `mngr-ssh-authority-in-vault.md`, `mngr-remove-init-via-dhcp.md`, `mngr-mirror-upstream-artifacts.md`

Gen-2 small follow-ups: `minds-admin` reads a tier's gen-2 management plane from the `[management_plane]` table of its `deploy.toml` instead of the deleted `management_plane.toml` (env deploy's proxy attach, the gen-2 prep's WireGuard peers and `:22` allowlist, the userspace-tunnel dial, and the `wireguard` commands, whose refusal messages now point at the table).

`minds-admin artifacts verify` now also probes each stored artifact's public mirror URL and reports `UNSERVED` (exit 1) when the bucket holds it but the live Worker does not serve it -- the Worker's route table deploys separately from the bucket's content, and the bucket-only check passed on 2026-09-09 while every artifact URL answered 400.

Gen-2 small follow-ups: `minds-admin server register` no longer refuses a delivered gen-2 box whose disk holds fewer than its RAM's full complement of default machines; it registers with a warning stating how many fit (the prep re-measures `disk_gb`, and the two-budget accounting fits fewer machines). `server order` keeps refusing such configs. The box-management dial now warns, rather than logging at debug, when the tier lists WireGuard operators but no operator key is at `~/.mindsadmin/<tier>/wireguard.key`, since a locked-down box is then unreachable with no visible reason.

`minds-admin env destroy` now refuses, before any remote teardown, while local processes still hold the env root -- a minds desktop backend launched with the env's `client.toml`, or a `mngr latchkey forward` supervisor owning the env's latchkey directory (detected through its lock) -- naming each with a stop hint; `--stop-local-processes` SIGTERMs them (desktop first, then the supervisor, whose teardown stops the gateway, `mngr observe`, and the tunnels) and waits for them to exit. Previously the destroy removed every remote resource under a still-running desktop and then failed at the very end because the mngr host dir was being written to while the env root was deleted.

`test_deployments.py services-against` now records the target env's pool in the run config -- the largest group of available rows sharing one template repo, ref, and region, read from the env's DB (`--pool-region` picks the region when several have rows) -- so the pool-backed tests (the fast-path create above all) run against an operator's dev env instead of skipping for lack of pool info.
